ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening for Politically Exposed Persons (PEP), OFAC SDN list, UN sanctions, and Spanish domestic sanctions lists in accordance with Ley 10/2010 and EU AML directives

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish language and Latin script; names must follow Spanish naming conventions and avoid prohibited terms
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying unlimited liability or public limited company without authorization

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Spain: consolidated text of the Capital Companies Act, approved by Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, 'LSC'), arts. 20-23, 28, 58-60, 62, 100, 124-127 and 210; Royal Decree 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil), arts. 116-124 and 327.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Mercantile Registry) for the name certificate; Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Mercantile Registry) of the province of the registered office for registration; electronic filing supported by CIRCE (Centro de Información y Red de Creación de Empresas).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución de sociedad limitada (public deed of incorporation of a limited liability company), subsequently inscribed in the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: For an S.L., the subscribed capital must be at least EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid at formation; payment is made in cash by deposit evidenced through a blocked bank deposit certificate issued by a Spanish credit institution. The statutory capital cannot be withdrawn except by lawful capital reductions. There is no separate public escrow requirement for an ordinary S.L., but the deposit certificate must remain in the company's formation account until registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
At the constitutive meeting held today, the undersigned shareholders resolved:

1. To subscribe fully the statutory share capital of EUR 3,000, represented by 3,000 equal participations of EUR 1 nominal value each, fully paid in cash and evidenced by the bank deposit certificate.

2. To approve the bylaws attached to the deed of incorporation and to execute that deed before a notary.

3. To adopt the registered office specified in Article 4 of the bylaws, Madrid, Spain, as the administrative seat and legal domicile.

4. To appoint [Name] as sole administrator, who accepts the office and will exercise the duties conferred by the Companies Act.

The minutes of this resolution are entered in the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain negative certificate of company name from the Central Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Paseo de la Castellana 281, Madrid) or CIRCE online portal (Sede electrónica del Registro Mercantil Central)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an official application (solicitud de certificación negativa de denominación) identifying the preferred corporate name and at least two alternative names. The Registry searches its database of existing Spanish companies and, if none conflicts, issues a negative name certificate valid for six months, preserving the name reservation.
required_dossiers: Solicitud de certificación negativa de denominación
List of preferred names in order
CIRCE digital certificate or electronic user credentials
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is refused because of name similarity, immediately resubmit using alternative names from the list or file a new application; no penalty is assessed for multiple name reservations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open provisional bank account and make the statutory capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution (Banco de España regulated entity) chosen by the promoters, with the account expressed in the name 'S.L. en constitución'
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Visit the bank with the negative name certificate and proposed bylaws; complete KYC verification for each promoter; open a provisional company formation account; deposit at least EUR 3,000; instruct the bank to block withdrawal of the capital until the company is registered; obtain a bank deposit certificate (certificado de depósito) identifying the depositors and amount payable to the notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide source-of-funds evidence and a sworn declaration; if the deposit certificate wording is not acceptable to the notary, ask the bank to re-issue it in the required notarial wording.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the public deed of incorporation before a Spanish notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the notarial district corresponding to the company's registered office (Colegio Notarial de Madrid or applicable province)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the name certificate, bank deposit certificate, promoters' identity documents, draft bylaws, and resolution to appoint administrator. The notary verifies legal capacity and legal compliance, then reads the deed and statutes. All incorporators sign, and the notary issues an original (copia autorizada) for subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: Notarial appointment via CIRCE or direct protocol request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary finds non-fatal defects, correct the statutory clauses or attach a signed rectification deed; if the notary declines the act because of identity or capacity issues, complete the evidence and re-appointment or instruct another notary in the same district.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain provisional NIF from the Spanish Tax Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), provincial taxation office; electronic filing via Sede Electrónica
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the deed is executed but before Mercantile registration, present the notarial first copy or special authorisation to AEAT to obtain the provisional NIF. Complete and submit Modelo 036 (census declaration) identifying the company in formation and the proposed administrator as person responsible for tax obligations.
required_dossiers: First copy of the public deed or notarial authorisation for NIF application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT rejects the application due to a mismatch in representative details or in Modelo 036, correct and re-submit through the Sede Electrónica; if the notarial digital certificate is not available, request an official transcript from the notary.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Spanish State Tax Administration Agency; electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a resident Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL): (i) obtain a provisional NIF (Numero de Identificacion Fiscal) before formal incorporation by filing Modelo 036 (Declaracion censal) with AEAT; (ii) execute the public deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitucion) before a Spanish Notary and register the SL in the Mercantile Registry; (iii) file the definitive Modelo 036/037 within one month of registration to finalize the NIF and register the commencement of business activities; (iv) NIF serves as the single corporate tax identification number for Corporate Income Tax, VAT, and customs purposes. For a foreign entity without a Spanish permanent establishment that is engaged in supplies to Spanish customers, a non-resident NIF must be applied for via Modelo 036, and a fiscal representative is mandatory for non-EU sellers under Article 84 bis of the Spanish VAT Law; for EU sellers, direct AEAT registration is permitted. No separate VAT registration number exists in Spain; the NIF is the sole VAT ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. An SL is a resident Spanish taxpayer under Article 7 of Ley 27/2014 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) subject to Corporate Income Tax at the standard rate of 25% on worldwide income, with no territorial scope limitation. The entity is a distinct taxable person for both Corporate Income Tax and VAT purposes and is not eligible for pass-through or check-the-box treatment under Spanish domestic law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a US-style check-the-box or pass-through election for an SL. Available statutory elections include: (i) Spanish tax group consolidation (Regimen de Consolidacion Fiscal) under Articles 56 et seq. LIS, available when the parent holds at least 70% of the subsidiary's capital; (ii) election for the special SME corporate income tax instalment regime; (iii) election for the EU VAT One-Stop-Shop (OSS) and Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) schemes for intra-EU distance sales and low-value imports; (iv) election for the simplified VAT small-business regime and the Recargo de Equivalencia retail surcharge regime, subject to turnover limits. Hybrid mismatch and ATAD rules are applied mandatorily without taxpayer election; no check-the-box hybrid election is available to recharacterise the SL as a transparent entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA - Impuesto sobre el Valor Anadido (Spanish Value Added Tax), transposed under Ley 37/1992 and implemented by Royal Decree 1624/1992, harmonised with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 - there is no general minimum turnover threshold for a resident SL engaged in economic activities; VAT registration is mandatory prior to the commencement of supplies. For online retail of consumer electronics by non-resident EU sellers making intra-community distance sales to Spanish consumers, the annual registration threshold is EUR 10,000 (excluding VAT) aggregated across the EU; once exceeded, VAT registration in Spain is mandatory. For non-EU sellers, registration is required from the first taxable supply unless the Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) or Union OSS is used. Spanish domestic simplified regimes apply only to small-effect activities generally below EUR 150,000 annual turnover, but retail sale of electronics falls under the Recargo de Equivalencia special scheme for retailers rather than under a general VAT exemption threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time VAT clearance applies through the Suministro Inmediato de Informacion (SII), which is mandatory for taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6,010,121.04 and certain other business regimes; SII requires transmission of invoice and billing register data to AEAT within 4 business days of issue or receipt via the AEAT electronic API using the SII XBRL/XML format. All resident businesses must use billing software compliant with Verifactu (Royal Decree 1007/2023), which requires the software to generate verifiable, tamper-proof invoice-digital-stamp records in XML or JSON with a unique alphanumeric hash signature; these records must be retained for 6 years. The Ley Crea y Crece (Ley 18/2022) mandates interoperable B2B electronic invoicing with accredited private platforms. No general QR-code mandatory stamping applies to all B2C invoices at present, but Verifactu's hash-based digital stamping provides fiscal clearance traceability.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: export of goods dispatched or transported outside the European Union is VAT-exempt (0%) under Article 21.5 of Ley 37/1992, subject to proof that the goods physically left EU territory within 3 months after dispatch; export may be evidenced by the customs export declaration and transport documents in the exporter's possession. The exemption also covers intra-EU supplies to VAT-registered businesses. Services: B2B and B2C services supplied to customers outside the EU are treated as outside the scope of Spanish VAT or zero-rated where the place of supply is outside Spain under Articles 69 and 70 of Ley 37/1992, provided the supplier retains evidence of the customer's non-EU residence and actual use of the service offshore where applicable. For online consumer electronics retail, the export zero-rating must be supported by the customs MRN number and delivery confirmation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - Documento Unico Administrativo (DUA) filed electronically with the AEAT Customs Authority, including the MRN (Movement Reference Number) and exit confirmation from the EU customs office.
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) or certificated carrier proof of dispatch evidencing physical departure of the goods from the EU.
Inward Remittance Certificate - bank certificate confirming receipt of the export payment in foreign currency or euros from the non-EU buyer.
Commercial invoice (factura comercial) expressly referring to the export exemption and the statutory basis.
Export packing list and purchase order details.
Proof of delivery (POD) / signed delivery confirmation from the end customer in the destination non-EU country.
Customs transit documentation (T1, ATR, or equivalent) where goods move through non-EU transit or a third territory before final destination.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False or improper use of the export zero-rating triggers retrospective clawback of the corresponding input VAT deducted on the related purchases, plus late-payment interest (interes de demora) at the statutory rate. Under Articles 191 to 197 of Ley 58/2003 (LGT), sanctions range from 50% to 150% of the VAT amount avoided, with aggravating factors for intentional concealment. Where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax period, criminal tax fraud under Article 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code applies, carrying imprisonment of up to 6 years and fines of up to six times the defrauded amount. AEAT audit focus on e-commerce exporters centres on the integrity of the export evidence trail, physical exit within the 3-month deadline, and the economic reality of the foreign recipient; documentation must be retained for at least 4 years (general tax limitation period) and 6 years under Verifactu invoice retention rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain adheres to full current-account convertibility under EU regulations. Capital-account movements are liberalized with no exchange controls. Profit remittances, dividends, and capital repatriation are unrestricted for Spanish SL entities provided AML/KYC compliance and beneficial-ownership disclosure are maintained.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds. Companies retain foreign-currency receipts after customs declaration. AML reporting required for transactions exceeding EUR 50,000; no statutory conversion timeline or ratio.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasible via licensed EMI partners (Stripe, PayPal) for EU and select LatAm corridors under Banco de España oversight; requires partnership with authorized institutions and full AML/KYC adherence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors and shareholders required for initial KYC and director interviews for new Spanish SL incorporations; remote video verification permitted for subsequent client onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds affidavits, clean legal opinions, and beneficial-ownership certificates

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity or high-risk jurisdiction links
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner register extracts and enhanced due-diligence transaction-purpose documentation

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Instant with purpose code 'CAPITAL_CONTRIBUTION' or 'EQUITY'. Verification requires board resolution, incorporation certificate, and source-of-funds evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing via SWIFT MT103 for international disbursements or issuance of commercial letters of credit. Trade settlements must reference purchase orders, comply with Incoterms, and satisfy export/import regulatory requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) - Modelo 200
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months and 25 days after the tax-closing date; for a calendar-year accounting period, no later than 25 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 5%/10%/15%/20% of the tax due depending on delay (Art. 27 LGT), plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75%); penalties of 50%-150% if filed after AEAT notification; habitual non-filing can lead to AEAT census deregistration and administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales) - Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Account, Notes, and, where applicable, Management Report and Cash-Flow Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (Commercial Registry) of the company's registered-office province
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must approve the accounts within 6 months of fiscal year-end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); deposit within 1 month after approval (by 30 July for a 31 December year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of €1,200 to €60,000 under Art. 283 LSC for failure to deposit for two consecutive years; automatic 'cierre registral' (blocking of all future registrations) until deposit is made; prolonged non-filing can lead to cancellation of the company's registration sheet and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Update or Confirmation to the Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro de Titularidades Reales - RTR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil / RTR administered with the Colegio de Registradores and the Ministry of Justice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing within 30 days of incorporation; updates within 30 days of any shareholding transfer or change in control; no standalone periodic UBO return when data is unchanged, but status is reconfirmed at each annual-accounts deposit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of €600 to €30,000 under Law 10/2010 for failure to communicate or update UBO data; the registry may block further filings until the RTR declaration is corrected; repeated violations are reported to SEPBLAC and may intensify AML supervisory action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months and 25 days after the fiscal year-end (by 25 July for calendar-year taxpayers); mandatory only when related-party transactions or related-party loans exceed €250,000 in the year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of €200 per datum (minimum €200, maximum €10,000) under Art. 198 LGT for late or incorrect informative returns; transfer-pricing adjustments may add substitution penalties of up to 75% of the tax advantage overlooked.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit when the SL meets at least two of the three following thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years at year-end: (i) total assets exceeding €2,850,000; (ii) annual net turnover exceeding €5,700,000; (iii) average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory for listed companies, credit institutions, insurance and investment undertakings, and any entity that belongs to a consolidated group, regardless of thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP - Plan General de Contabilidad (PGC), as approved by Real Decreto 1514/2007, with the simplified PGC-PYMES (Real Decreto 1515/2007) available to companies meeting small-company limits (assets ≤ €4,000,000; turnover ≤ €8,000,000; employees ≤ 50). Consolidated groups apply IFRS as adopted by the EU (IFRS-EU). Deposition format must comply with the official standard sheets of the Mercantile Registry; accounting and tax records must be retained for at least 7 years.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 10/2010 and Real Decreto 304/2014, the SL must file beneficial-ownership details in the RTR upon incorporation and within 30 days of any qualifying shareholding transfer or change of control. For an SL with unchanged ownership, the UBO information is reconfirmed as part of the annual accounts deposit and in the annual corporate-tax return; there is no separate periodic UBO confirmation form. Directors are personally liable for keeping the shareholders' register and UBO file accurate and up to date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Contracts with Directors and Shareholders (Libro Registro de Contratos)
Inventory and Annual Accounts Book (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $2,000 - $5,500 per year for a small or medium SL if the statutory audit threshold is met
